_readme: THE SKILL LOCK. One entry per skill directory whose bytes someone has actually read.
A skill is not a library. A library is code a sandbox runs; a skill is PROSE THE MODEL
FOLLOWS AS INSTRUCTION, so installing one is closer to granting edit access to your system
prompt than to `npm install`. This file cannot make a skill safe. It guarantees one narrower
thing: nothing changes SILENTLY. Read docs/reference/skill-safety/ before adding an entry.
SHIPPED EMPTY, ON PURPOSE. A lock inherited from someone else's machine pins someone else's
review. `skills` is yours to fill as you vendor skills, and it stays empty until you do.
ENTRY SHAPE — hand-write the first five fields, then let --update compute the rest:
source        where the skill came from: a repository URL, or `local`
sourceType    git | release | local
skillPath     the path WITHIN that source, so the review is reproducible
skillDir      the path in THIS repo, relative to the root. Point it at the TRACKED copy
(.agents/skills/<name>), never at a gitignored live mirror: an entry that
pins bytes a clone does not contain fails the gate on checkout, before
anyone has touched a skill, and the documented way to clear that is
--update, the one action that must never be reflexive.
reviewedAt    YYYY-MM-DD, the day a HUMAN read every line of it. --update moves this date
only when the digest moved, because the value of a review date is that it is
false to move it.
computedHash  sha256 over the whole directory — written by --update
fileDigests   per-file sha256, so a drift report can NAME the changed file — by --update
hashAlgo      `sha256-dir-v2`. The algorithm is documented in skill-verify.cjs because v1's
was not, which is why v1's digests could never be reproduced from disk.
`pluginPins` is an optional sibling of `skills`, for marketplace plugins installed OUTSIDE
this repo: { "<plugin-id>": { "sha": "<commit>", "reviewedAt": "YYYY-MM-DD", "note": "…" } }.
It is absent here because nothing is pinned. An enabled plugin with no pin is reported every
session as uncovered rather than clean — this lock cannot secure files it does not contain.
Commit this file in the SAME commit as the skill it describes. A vendoring commit that does
not touch the lock did not go through the checklist, which makes compliance greppable.
node scripts/harness/guards/skill-verify.cjs --check     the verdict, with a GATE line
node scripts/harness/guards/skill-verify.cjs --update    re-baseline, AFTER reading the diff
